source_text.Q-1011: LOW (INV-10 family), S3, ISS-1026 follow-up, GH #2311, local ISS-1029 (queue issue_ref ISS-1011 clashes with local ISS-1011). Six acceptance criteria in queue task 1011.

task.description: WF-03 Steps 0.5+1+2 for Q-1011 / GH #2311 / ISS-1029: registry lookup, run the repro, root cause, fix design for the three promotion read routes (stored-tenant check), list decision, test update list, draft docs/issues/ISS-1029.yaml. Design only; no lib/ code.

result.summary:
DIAGNOSIS (code path confirmed by reading every involved function; the dynamic repro could NOT be run here, see REPRO STATUS). The gap is real and unguarded. In lib/letflow/routers/promotions.ex the three read handlers never look at the stored plan's source_tenant_id / target_tenant_id: handle_get_assertion_run (L487) calls PromotionReviewStore.get_review/2 and, on {:ok, _}, returns Definitions.get_latest_assertion_run (run status, counts, failing_assertion_ids); handle_context (L526) calls get_review/2 and renders review_context_map/2 (status, requested_by, def_type, def_id, created_at, row_version; serialised_plan is only SHAPED by shape_plan/2 for a non-operator, ISS-1021/1023, never refused); handle_list_reviews (L1157) calls PromotionReviewStore.list_reviews/2 (lib/letflow/definitions/promotion_review_store.ex L239) and renders every row in the caller's schema. The write handlers (approve L572, reject L613, apply L653, run-assertions L788) call stored_tenants_authorized?/3 (L678) first and answer Response.not_found/1 for a foreign-named, malformed or legacy plan. The authz_get macros (L225-L260) only gate :PromotionsRead; the per-review decision is missing. Same root cause as ISS-1026 (check added to writes only), on the read side. Why no test caught it: ISS-1021/1023 tests deliberately asserted 200 plus shaped bodies for foreign-named reviews (shaping was the control), and ISS-1026's repro covered writes only.

REPRO STATUS: test/letflow/routers/promotion_read_stored_ids_test.exs (HEAD d2e08c67b) was run as `LETFLOW_DB_PORT=5499 MIX_ENV=test mix test <file>` under the machine mutex at 2026-10-13T11:27:46Z and could not start: `tcp connect (localhost:5499): connection refused`, `** (Mix) The database for Letflow.Repo couldn't be created: killed`. Environment: Docker daemon not running (dockerDesktopLinuxEngine pipe missing), nothing listening on 5432/5462/5499, Windows service postgresql-x64-17 is Stopped and Start-Service is denied (no admin). So there is NO measured failure to quote. Static expectation (NOT measured): the 3 tests in describe "non-operator reader, review naming a foreign tenant in its own schema" fail (context and GET /:id return 200 instead of the 404 baseline bytes; the list contains the review id) and the 2 control tests pass. The first real mix run (TEST-RUNNER / ELIXIR-DEV with a reachable DB) must confirm the 3-red/2-green split and quote it.

REGISTRY (Step 0.5): ISS-1026 (resolved; approve/reject; its follow_ups name this issue; its fix is the pattern to copy), ISS-1021 (context plan allowlist) and ISS-1023 (entries withheld) are resolved predecessors, not recurrences: none touched the read gate. docs/issues has no ISS-1029; the queue issue_ref for Q-1011 is ISS-1011 which collides with local ISS-1011 (SwiftRoute roster), so local id ISS-1029 is kept (cited by ISS-1026 follow_ups and decision 0046 ~L470); no origin branch or queue ref uses 1029.

FIX DESIGN (lib/ in two files; no migration, no new route or response shape)

A. Predicate. Extract the decision core of stored_tenants_authorized?/3 (L678-L696) into a pure private fun review_tenants_authorized?(conn, %PromotionReview{serialised_plan: s}): decode s (non-map or malformed -> %{}), then tenants_authorized?(conn, [plan["source_tenant_id"], plan["target_tenant_id"]]) (L315, i.e. Letflow.Api.TenantTarget.authorize_target_tenant/2: platform_scope? -> :ok, else each id must be a canonical UUID equal to the caller's tenant, case-insensitive). stored_tenants_authorized?/3 becomes get_review + review_tenants_authorized?/2 (and true on :review_not_found), so approve/reject/apply/run-assertions are byte-identical and all seven routes share one predicate. Minimal-diff alternative with equal behaviour: call stored_tenants_authorized?/3 unchanged before the read (one extra get_review per request). Prefer the extraction: one read, no check/render gap.

B. GET /promotions/:id/context (handle_context L526): read the review once; if {:ok, review} and not review_tenants_authorized?(conn, review) -> Response.not_found(conn); else render_context as today. shape_plan/2 stays UNCHANGED (defence in depth, INV-2).

C. GET /promotions/:id (handle_get_assertion_run L487): same gate on the {:ok, review} branch BEFORE Definitions.get_latest_assertion_run is called. Non-UUID and nonexistent ids already take {:error, :review_not_found} -> 404, so all denial causes emit the same Response.not_found(conn) bytes.

D. GET /promotions (handle_list_reviews L1157 + PromotionReviewStore.list_reviews/2 L239). DECISION: OMIT, not placeholder, and NO scan cap (revision 1, CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR F3). A placeholder discloses existence, count and ordering of the hidden row and changes the 7-key item contract. A router-side Enum.filter would break pagination, and a SQL filter is unsafe (serialised_plan is :text; a ::jsonb cast raises on malformed legacy rows and would 500 the whole list). So filter inside the store's keyset loop:
 - list_reviews/2 takes a new optional opts key :row_visible? . Widen the @spec/@type opts to [prefix: String.t(), row_visible?: (PromotionReview.t() -> boolean())]. Contract: absent or nil = no filtering (existing behaviour and store tests unchanged); a 1-arity fun = filter; any other value raises ArgumentError (fail closed, never silently unfiltered; a guard `is_nil(f) or is_function(f, 1)`). The router passes fn r -> review_tenants_authorized?(conn, r) end ONLY when tenant_view(conn) != :operator; the operator path is structurally the current one.
 - Algorithm (exact): chunk_size = max(page_size + 1, 100) (module attribute @min_scan_chunk 100). Loop: fetch chunk_size rows with the existing ordering (desc inserted_at, desc id) and keyset seek, SQL filters (status/def_id/def_type) applied first; keep rows where row_visible?.(row), appending to the accumulated visible list; stop as soon as the accumulated list holds page_size + 1 rows, OR the chunk returned fewer than chunk_size rows (table exhausted); otherwise seek after the last row of the chunk (scanned, hidden or not, used ONLY as an in-memory seek inside this one request) and fetch again. There is no scan cap and no row budget: the scan ends by exhaustion or by filling the page. Memory is bounded by page_size + 1 visible rows plus one chunk.
   * accumulated >= page_size + 1: page = first page_size, next_cursor = build_list_reviews_next_cursor(last EMITTED row) (existing call).
   * otherwise (exhausted): page = all visible rows, next_cursor = nil. A hidden-only remainder therefore yields items [] / next_cursor nil, the same bytes as an empty list.
 - Consequence and invariants (binding): (i) every next_cursor ever returned encodes only the id and inserted_at of a row that was EMITTED to this caller, i.e. a visible row; a hidden row's id/inserted_at is never in a cursor, never in a body; (ii) no visible row is skipped or made unreachable by hidden rows, however many hidden rows precede it; (iii) an empty page never carries a non-nil next_cursor (so clients that stop on an empty page, and clients that page on next_cursor presence, both behave correctly; the web client web/src/pages/promotions/PromotionReviewListPage.tsx L72/L155 pages on next_cursor presence and its stack never receives an empty-page cursor); (iv) the response is observationally identical to the same list in a schema that never had the hidden rows (except for timing).
 - Trade-off (accepted, stated for SECURITY-REVIEWER): worst-case cost of one non-operator list request is a full keyset scan of that tenant's promotion_reviews, JSON-decoding each scanned plan. Review rows are human-approved promotion requests (low volume) and foreign-named rows exist only for operator-created or legacy rows in a non-platform schema; the scan runs only after Authorize/rate limits and only for non-operators. A capped alternative was rejected: any cap forces either a cursor anchored on a hidden row (discloses its id/inserted_at, cursors are unsigned base64) or one anchored on the last visible row (makes visible rows behind a hidden run > cap unreachable, a livelock) or an empty page with a cursor (observable difference). If volume ever makes the scan a concern, the fix is a stored own_tenant_visible column written at insert (separate issue), not a cap.
 - Cursor format, expiry, wrong_endpoint, invalid_cursor handling unchanged; cursors minted before the fix remain valid (they encode an emitted, hence visible, row).

E. Operator unchanged: the predicate returns :ok for platform_scope? (PLATFORM_ADMIN of the pinned platform tenant) and the list passes no filter.

TEST CHANGES (exact list; re-swept: every test file in test/ that references Promotions.call, "/promotions", insert_review, seed_review! or req397_sample_plan was checked, including those the validator listed as unaffected)
1. Extend test/letflow/routers/promotion_read_stored_ids_test.exs (existing 5 stay). New tests, all comparing against the nonexistent-id baseline bytes via Scope.observable/1:
 (a) GET /:id for a foreign-named review that HAS an assertion run: 404 baseline bytes, body holds no run id, no failing_assertion_ids, no assertions_failed.
 (b) non-UUID id on both per-review routes: unchanged 404.
 (c) LIST paging with hidden rows interleaved at page boundaries: page_size 1 and 2; visible rows V, hidden rows H arranged V H V, H H V V, V H H; pages hold only visible ids, union of pages == visible set exactly once each, final next_cursor nil, a hidden-only tail gives items [] and next_cursor nil.
 (d) LIST cursor non-disclosure (F3): for every page of (c), base64url-decode next_cursor (Pagination.decode_cursor or Base.url_decode64) and assert it contains none of the hidden review ids and none of their inserted_at microsecond values; also assert no page that is empty has a non-nil cursor.
 (e) LIST long hidden run (kills any scan cap): seed one visible row oldest, then 250 hidden rows newer (more than two 100-row chunks), page_size 1 as non-operator: the first request already returns the visible row with next_cursor nil (one request, no empty page), and the same with the visible row in the middle (hidden run of 250 on each side).
 (f) LIST malformed/legacy rows (F4): in the reader's own schema seed own/own rows plus rows overwritten (overwrite_plan! recipe of promotion_context_entries_scope_test.exs L291+) to: JSON string "x", array [1], number 7, null, truncated/invalid JSON text '{"a":', and a map missing the ids; as a non-operator assert status 200 (never 500), only the own/own rows listed, ordered and paged consistently at page_size 1; as the operator assert the same rows appear in the list unfiltered (operator sees all rows, the list item map does not read the plan).
 (g) LIST filters compose: status filter and def_id filter with hidden rows present return only visible rows of that status/def.
 (h) LIST operator includes the foreign-named review (200, listed) with next_cursor identical in shape to today.
 (i) AC4 platform-tenant-held non-operator reader (F2): TENANT_ADMIN of P (Fixture.router_conn(..., ctx.p, ["TENANT_ADMIN"], ...)) with the pin on P AND with the pin unset (Fixture.unpin!/pin!), reading an operator-seeded review Scope.seed_review!(ctx.p, a, b) in P's schema: GET /:id and GET /:id/context answer the nonexistent baseline bytes; GET / omits it while an own-tenant Scope.seed_review!(ctx.p, p, p) review stays listed; operator (PLATFORM_ADMIN of pinned P) reads the foreign-named review 200 on all three routes.
2. test/letflow/definitions/promotion_review_store_test.exs (store level): row_visible? nil unchanged; all hidden; boundary page; long hidden run over 2 chunks; a predicate that raises propagates (documented: the router predicate itself never raises); non-1-arity value raises ArgumentError; cursor from a filtered call decodes to an emitted row.
3. UPDATE existing tests that assert a non-operator 200 on a review whose stored ids are foreign or absent (flip to the nonexistent-review 404 bytes, keep operator controls, drop shaping assertions unreachable for such reviews):
 - promotion_context_shaping_test.exs (T-8): context_omits_foreign_tenant_ids_for_non_operator (L57, b->a read as A), context_other_keys_and_status_unchanged (L115, b->a). Keep context_unknown_top_level_keys_dropped_and_entries_not_descended (a/a) and context_unchanged_for_operator.
 - promotion_context_allowlist_test.exs (T-11): foreign_side_definition_id_omitted_own_side_kept (L167: cases b/a, a/b, b/b become 404; only a/a stays 200), null_definition_id_omitted_for_foreign_side_kept_for_own_side (L206, b->a), non_map_plan_fails_closed (L221: non-operator half 404, operator half unchanged), legacy_plan_missing_keys (L240: non-operator halves 404, operator halves unchanged), entries_not_a_list_replaced_by_empty_list (L265: stored JSON has NO tenant ids), non_scalar_under_plain_key_omitted (L129, ADDED in revision 1, BLOCKER F1: stored JSON {process_key, base_version, entries} has NO tenant ids; the non-operator read becomes 404. Preferred rewrite: put own a/a ids into `stored` so the plain-key omission is still asserted at 200, and keep raw-body refutation of b; the alternative of flipping to 404 loses the coverage of the plain-key rule), envelope_has_nine_keys_for_both_views (L322: fixture a reads b->a so 404; operator p half stays 200), pin_unset_would_be_operator_is_shaped_like_everyone_else (L336: unpinned p reading b->p, becomes 404). For the two tests that gain own ids (entries_not_a_list..., non_scalar_under_plain_key...) the ids in the JSON must be the reader's own tenant id (ctx.a.tenant_id) for BOTH source_tenant_id and target_tenant_id. Unchanged: odd_tenant_keys_never_reach_a_non_operator (a/a seed), unknown_top_level_key_omitted (a/a), entries_kept_exactly_as_stored (a/a), own_tenant_ids_kept_case_insensitively (a/a), nil_tenant_context_never_reaches_the_handler (500 from Authorize before the handler), operator_sees_all_unchanged.
 - promotion_context_entries_scope_test.exs (T-13): foreign_reviews_entries_are_empty_for_a_non_operator_reader_in_p (L173, B/C, C/B, B/B), one_foreign_side_is_enough_to_withhold_entries (L195: foreign cases 404; P/P control stays 200 with entries), withheld_entries_leave_the_rest_of_the_response_unchanged (L262), legacy_plans_with_missing_or_non_binary_tenant_ids_fail_closed (L292: non-operator 404, operator view unchanged), tenant_admin_of_the_platform_tenant_reads_a_foreign_review_without_entries (L400: 404 pinned and unpinned, operator control unchanged). Unchanged: operator_reads_the_same_foreign_review..., own_tenant_reviews_still_show_entries, own_ids_case_insensitive_keep_entries, the AC5 403 tripwire.
 - promotions_test.exs (REQ-397 list tests; broken by the fix though not named in the AC): req397_sample_plan/2 (L375) stamps source_tenant_id: Ecto.UUID.generate() with target = caller's tenant and reads as TENANT_ADMIN, so every R12 list test (~L437-L720) would find its rows omitted. Change the helper to source_tenant_id: tenant_id (own/own); no assertion change (validator verified no assertion mentions source_tenant_id).
 - Verified UNAFFECTED: req077_promotion_pipeline_test.exs R3/R4 (default PLATFORM_ADMIN, pinned), req446_cross_tenant_denial_test.exs (identifier rows b/b, list baseline a/a), tenant_admin_routes_test.exs L149 (a/a), promotion_approve_reject_stored_ids_test.exs (writes only), promotion_scope_test.exs (nonexistent ids, writes), platform-events tests (other route), promotion_review_store_test.exs existing cases (no row_visible?).
4. Docs: test/specs/ISS-1029.md (new: criterion-to-test table, mutants, measured run), notes appended to test/specs/ISS-1021.md and test/specs/ISS-1023.md (foreign-id shaping now defence in depth behind the 404), docs/migration/decisions/0046-admin-scopes-and-role-charter.md ~L470 (close the follow-up), docs/issues/ISS-1029.yaml -> resolved with the real run id.

MUTANTS (each applied alone must fail the named tests): M1 gate removed from handle_context -> context repro and flipped T-8/T-11/T-13 tests, 1(i). M2 gate removed from handle_get_assertion_run -> GET /:id repro, 1(a), 1(i). M3 list passes no row_visible? -> list repro, 1(c), 1(f), 1(i). M4 REMOVED (equivalent: get_latest_assertion_run is a pure read, same bytes; ordering is checked in REVIEW, not by a test). M5 predicate uses `or` over the two ids -> one_foreign_side_is_enough, (own source, foreign target) repro seed. M6 operator also filtered -> 1(h), operator controls. M7 placeholder instead of omit -> list repro, 1(c). M8 next_cursor built from the last SCANNED row instead of the last EMITTED row on a full page -> 1(d) (the +1 hidden row appears in the cursor) and 1(c) duplicates/skips. M9 filter applied after the page cut (router-side Enum.filter) -> 1(c) short pages, 1(e). M10 predicate fails open on a malformed plan -> single-review legacy cases and 1(f). M11 predicate raises on a malformed plan (Jason.decode! instead of Jason.decode) -> 1(f) (list 500). M12 scan stops after one chunk or after N rows (a cap reintroduced) -> 1(e) (visible row behind 250 hidden rows not returned) and 1(c). M13 non-1-arity row_visible? silently ignored -> store test (ArgumentError expected). M14 cursor on exhaustion non-nil after a hidden-only tail -> 1(c)/(d) (empty page with cursor).

RISKS: (R1) shape_plan/2 foreign branches become dead for non-operators through the route; kept deliberately (defence in depth, operator with pin unset); deleting them is a separate change. (R2) worst-case per-request full scan for non-operators (see D trade-off); no cap by design; revisit with a stored column if volume warrants. (R3) per-row JSON decode inside the scan: non-operators only, bounded by table size. (R4) a review the caller legitimately created as operator in its own schema naming foreign tenants becomes invisible to that caller once it is no longer an operator; intended and consistent with approve/reject/apply. (R5) ordering vs REQ-447: this lands before :PromotionsRead goes to TENANT_ADMIN/TENANT_AUDITOR, the intended order. (R6) SECURITY-REVIEWER gate required (tenant-data path, INV-10), AC6. (R7) timing: a list request that hides rows is slower than one that does not (scan cost); not byte-observable, accepted, SECURITY-REVIEWER to confirm.

ROUTING: size S3 and fully specified, so CODE-DESIGNER may write only a short design (lib/letflow/design/iss1029-read-stored-ids.md) -> CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (re-run) -> ELIXIR-DEV (promotions.ex, promotion_review_store.ex) + TEST-DESIGNER (tests above) -> SECURITY-REVIEWER -> REVIEWER -> TEST-RUNNER (Postgres on 5462: LETFLOW_DEV_DB_CONFIRMED=1 MIX_ENV=test mix test <file>) -> RELEASE-VALIDATOR.

REVISION 1 (2026-10-13, after CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR FAIL, step-02): F1 BLOCKER non_scalar_under_plain_key_omitted added, test tree re-swept; F2 MAJOR AC4 P-held TENANT_ADMIN reader added for /:id and list (1(i)); F3 MAJOR cap removed, cursor invariant stated, tests 1(d)/(e), mutants M8/M12/M14; F4 MAJOR list-level malformed-row test 1(f), mutant M11; F5 MINOR chunk/exhaustion semantics, @spec widening, web client call site named; F6 MINOR M4 dropped; F7 MINOR affected_files in ISS-1029.yaml extended.
REPRO NOTE: the validator measured the repro at 4daad8ca0 against Postgres 5462: 'Result: 2/5 passed, Failed: 3 tests', the 3-red/2-green split predicted above (GET /:id/context answered 200 instead of the 404 baseline). That measurement supersedes the static expectation in REPRO STATUS.
